annotations.title: Why a build failed, and the fix

description: Says why a build failed, as one cause and the step that fixes it, instead of a log: from the newest failed run of this app (or releaseId), and, when given, the build's log (logPath, a file on this computer, or text pasted from GitHub's or Cloud Build's log). It knows the usual ones: disk or memory, the Gradle wrapper committed from Windows, the JDK or Android SDK, CocoaPods, an old Xcode, signing and capabilities, a build number already used, Google Play's target SDK, missing node modules or Flutter, build files git doesn't have, GitHub's billing, and the network or a busy store. A transient one says so: start the same build again with ploa_release_start (say first when it costs the person minutes). When it doesn't know the failure, it says so and gives the error to read.

dir.description: The app's folder (absolute path). Defaults to the folder the agent runs in.

logPath.description: Absolute path to the build's log on this computer (the CLI prints it: full log: …).

releaseId.description: The failed release, as ploa_runs lists them. Default: this app's newest failed run.

text.description: The end of a log, pasted (GitHub Actions, Cloud Build).

name: ploa_build_diagnose
